description: Find location slug ids and centroids to search by.

parameters.name: input
parameters.description:
**Partial place name to look up.** Required. Type-ahead friendly  -  2-3 characters is enough.

- Ex: `Austin`  -  matches Austin TX, Austin MN, Austin IN, …
- Ex: `787`  -  matches Austin-area ZIP codes
- Ex: `Upper West Side`  -  matches the neighborhood in Manhattan (and in Buffalo)
- Ex: `Travis`  -  matches Travis County, TX

**This is the lookup endpoint you should call first.** Each suggestion carries the identifiers the other endpoints need:

1. `centroid.lat` / `centroid.lon` → feed straight into `/search-by-coordinates`
2. `slug_id` → feed into `/neighborhood-info` (neighborhoods) or `/market-hotness` (ZIPs). This matters because slugs are hard to guess  -  the Upper West Side is `Upper-West-Side_Manhattan_NY`, using the borough rather than `New-York`.
3. `city` + `state_code` → feed into `/market-feed`, `/geo-statistics`, `/property-search`
4. `postal_code` → feed into `/mortgage-rates`, `/market-hotness`, `/map-boundary`

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
**Maximum number of suggestions to return.** Optional  -  default `10`, range `1`-`50`.

Results are ordered by relevance score (`_score`), so the first suggestion is almost always the intended one. Use `5` for a type-ahead dropdown, or a larger value when disambiguating a common name across states.

Ex: `5`, `10` (default), `25`.

parameters.name: area_types
parameters.description:
**Restrict results to specific geography kinds.** Optional  -  all kinds are returned when omitted.

- `city`  -  a city or town
- `postal_code`  -  a 5-digit ZIP
- `neighborhood`  -  a named neighborhood within a city
- `county`  -  a US county
- `state`  -  a US state
- `address`  -  a specific street address
- `school` / `school_district`  -  schools and districts

Ex: `area_types=city,postal_code` to offer only cities and ZIPs; `area_types=neighborhood` when you specifically need a neighborhood `slug_id`.

Multiple values allowed  -  a suggestion matching **ANY** of them is returned. Comma-separated.

description: Search US homes for sale / rent / sold with rich filters and pagination.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description:
**Free-text location  -  the simplest way to search.** Accepts anything Realtor.com autocomplete
handles, and resolves it to the right geography for you.

- `Austin, TX`  -  city + state
- `78701`  -  ZIP code
- `Travis County, TX`  -  county
- `Downtown, Austin, TX`  -  neighborhood
- `9504 Quail Village Ln, Austin, TX 78758`  -  full street address

**Precedence:** free-text `location` overrides `city` / `state_code` / `postal_code` / `county` /
`neighborhood`  -  send one style or the other, not both.

A search AREA (`lat`+`lon` radius, or `polygon`) **intersects** with whatever location you also pass  - 
it does not replace it. A 5-mile downtown-Austin radius returns 2,693 homes alone, 2,661 with
`location=Austin, TX`, and **0** with `location=Round Rock, TX`  -  correctly zero, because that radius
reaches no Round Rock homes. So only add a location to a radius/polygon search when you genuinely want
both constraints.

`lat`/`lon`, `polygon` and a `commute_lat`/`commute_lon` isochrone are three ways of drawing the SAME
thing  -  one search area  -  so no two of them can be combined (400).

**Commute is the one exception**, and it is a trap upstream: a free-text `location` is silently IGNORED
when a commute origin is set, so `location=Round Rock, TX` with an Austin commute origin would hand back
Austin homes with no warning. This API rejects that combination with a 400  -  use `city` + `state_code`
(or `postal_code`) instead, which correctly intersects with the isochrone.

Case-insensitive  -  `tx` and `TX` behave identically. Ignored when `location` is set.

- `-80.1918`  -  Miami, FL

parameters.name: radius_miles
parameters.description:
**Search radius in miles** around the `lat` / `lon` centre point.

Default `5` when omitted. Maximum `50`  -  a larger radius is rejected upstream.

How much a radius widens the result set (Austin, TX centre `30.2672,-97.7431`, `for_sale`):
- `1`  -  326 homes
- `2`  -  977 homes
- `5`  -  2,762 homes
- `10`  -  5,383 homes
- `25`  -  18,410 homes
- `50`  -  37,421 homes (the cap)

Ignored unless BOTH `lat` and `lon` are supplied.

parameters.name: commute_lat
parameters.description:
**Latitude of the commute origin**  -  the place you want to travel FROM, typically a workplace or a
school. Homes are then filtered to whatever is reachable from it inside `commute_minutes`.

Required together with `commute_lon`: one without the other returns a 400.

- `30.2672`  -  downtown Austin, TX
- `40.7128`  -  Lower Manhattan, New York, NY
- `25.7617`  -  downtown Miami, FL

Range `-90` to `90`.

**Mutually exclusive with the `lat` / `lon` / `radius_miles` radius search and with `polygon`**  -  the
isochrone IS the search area, and upstream accepts exactly one. Sending a commute together with either
of them returns a 400.

**On its own, the isochrone is not bounded by any city.** A 60-minute drive out of downtown Austin
spills well past the city limits, so it can return MORE homes than Austin itself has: 14,309 reachable
for-sale listings against an Austin baseline of 7,425. That is correct  -  the extra homes are in
Round Rock, Kyle, Georgetown and the rest of the metro.

**Adding a location INTERSECTS with the isochrone**, it does not widen it. The same 30-minute drive
returns 6,261 homes on its own but 5,600 when combined with `location=Austin, TX`  -  you get only the
homes that are both inside Austin and inside the travel-time band. Leave the location off when you want
"anywhere I can reach in N minutes"; add one when you want "inside this city AND reachable in N minutes".

`/search-by-commute` is the dedicated endpoint for this filter and requires the pair up front.

parameters.name: commute_minutes
parameters.description:
**Travel-time budget for the commute isochrone, in minutes.** Default: `30` when omitted.

A CLOSED set of six values  -  anything else (`15`, `45`, `90`, …) is rejected with a 400:

- `10`  -  10 minutes (Austin, TX by car: 2,258 for-sale homes)
- `20`  -  20 minutes
- `30`  -  30 minutes, the default (Austin, TX by car: 6,262 · on foot: 1,777)
- `40`  -  40 minutes
- `50`  -  50 minutes
- `60`  -  60 minutes (Austin, TX by car: 14,310  -  nearly double the 7,426-listing Austin
  baseline, because an hour of driving leaves the city entirely)

Ignored unless BOTH `commute_lat` and `commute_lon` are supplied.

parameters.name: commute_transport
parameters.description:
**How the commute is travelled.** Default: `drive` when omitted.

- `drive`  -  by car (default). Austin, TX 30-minute isochrone: 6,262 for-sale homes
- `walk`  -  on foot. Austin, TX 30-minute isochrone: 1,777 for-sale homes

**Only these two modes actually work.** `cycle` and `public_transport` exist in the upstream
enum but are **unwired**: they are accepted and then silently ignored, returning the FULL
unfiltered result set as though no commute filter had been applied (verified  -  Austin for-sale
returns the same 7,425 at every interval, byte-identical to sending no commute at all).

This API rejects them with a 400 rather than pass that through, because a silently-unfiltered
page of results is far more damaging than an error: you would believe you were seeing homes
within a 30-minute bike ride and actually be seeing the whole metro.

Ignored unless BOTH `commute_lat` and `commute_lon` are supplied.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
**Listing lifecycle bucket.** Defaults to `for_sale` when omitted.

- `for_sale`  -  active for-sale listings (Austin, TX: 7,593)
- `for_rent`  -  active rentals (Austin, TX: 7,283)
- `sold`  -  closed sales (Austin, TX: 126,013)
- `ready_to_build`  -  builder plans / buildable lots
- `off_market`  -  no longer actively listed
- `other`  -  everything else Realtor.com tracks

Validated upstream: an unknown token returns a 400 listing the valid values.

**Tip:** `/properties-for-sale`, `/properties-for-rent` and `/properties-sold` pin this for you,
so you never have to send it there.

For the finer-grained status the listing agent set in the MLS itself  -  Active vs Pending vs Sold  - 
use `mls_status`.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

parameters.name: mls_status
parameters.description:
**Status the listing agent set in the source MLS**  -  a finer signal than `status`.

`status` is the Realtor.com lifecycle bucket (`for_sale`, `sold`, …); `mls_status` is what the

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description:
**Raw feature tags**, merged straight into the upstream tag filter.

**Warning  -  this is an OPEN vocabulary that is NOT validated upstream.** A typo or an
unrecognised tag does not raise an error: it silently returns **0 results**. (`zzz_not_a_tag`
returns 0, not a 400.)

**Use the five validated group parameters instead**  -  every token they accept is verified live,
and a bad one gets a helpful 400:
- `heating_cooling`  -  Central Air, Central Heat, Forced Air, Energy Efficient
- `home_features`  -  Fireplace, Hardwood Floors, Swimming Pool, Basement, …
- `lot_features`  -  Waterfront, Corner Lot, Cul de Sac, Lake View, …
- `community_features`  -  Community Pool, Clubhouse, Golf, Security, …
- `nyc_amenities`  -  Doorman, Elevator, Dishwasher, Outdoor Space

All five groups plus `tags` merge into ONE upstream tag array (union, de-duplicated), so they can
be mixed freely in a single request.

Only reach for `tags` when you need a tag you have actually seen in a `/search` response  -  every
result echoes its own `tags` array. Examples: `central_air`, `fireplace`, `swimming_pool`, `view`.

Multiple values allowed, but they are combined with **AND**  -  a listing must have EVERY value listed, so each extra value NARROWS the result set. (Verified in Austin, TX: `swimming_pool` alone ~1,100 listings, `fireplace` alone ~3,000, both together 696.) Comma-separated.

parameters.name: selling_agent_name
parameters.description:
**Full name of the agent on the SELLING side of the transaction.**

**Exact, whole-name match**  -  there is no partial, prefix or fuzzy matching. `Guadalupe` does not
find `Guadalupe Abbud`; spell the name exactly as Realtor.com holds it, including middle initials
and suffixes.

Verified: `selling_agent_name=Guadalupe Abbud` returns 3 listings.

Get the exact spelling from `/agents-search`, or from the `advertisers[]` block of any property
detail. A name that matches nobody returns 0 results, not an error  -  so an empty response usually
means the spelling is off.

**Prefer `fulfillment_id` whenever you have it:** an advertiser id is stable and unambiguous,
while two agents can share a name and the same agent can be spelled differently across MLSs.

parameters.name: fulfillment_id
parameters.description:
**Realtor.com advertiser id of an agent**  -  the cleanest way to pull one agent's entire book of
business.

Unlike `selling_agent_name`, this works on EVERY status. Verified for agent `3809719`:

- `status=for_sale`  -  70 listings
- `status=for_rent`  -  10 listings
- `status=sold`  -  383 listings
- `status=off_market`  -  9 listings

Where to get one:

- `/agents-search`  -  every agent row echoes its own `fulfillment_id`
- any property detail  -  `advertisers[].fulfillment_id`

Examples: `fulfillment_id=3809719` (one agent), `fulfillment_id=3809719,1715146` (a whole team in a
single call).

An id that matches no listings returns 0 results rather than a 400  -  it is not validated against the
agent directory. `/agent-listings` is the dedicated endpoint for this filter.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

location.description:
**Free-text location  -  the simplest way to search.** Accepts anything Realtor.com autocomplete
handles, and resolves it to the right geography for you.

- `Austin, TX`  -  city + state
- `78701`  -  ZIP code
- `Travis County, TX`  -  county
- `Downtown, Austin, TX`  -  neighborhood
- `9504 Quail Village Ln, Austin, TX 78758`  -  full street address

**Precedence:** free-text `location` overrides `city` / `state_code` / `postal_code` / `county` /
`neighborhood`  -  send one style or the other, not both.

A search AREA (`lat`+`lon` radius, or `polygon`) **intersects** with whatever location you also pass  - 
it does not replace it. A 5-mile downtown-Austin radius returns 2,693 homes alone, 2,661 with
`location=Austin, TX`, and **0** with `location=Round Rock, TX`  -  correctly zero, because that radius
reaches no Round Rock homes. So only add a location to a radius/polygon search when you genuinely want
both constraints.

`lat`/`lon`, `polygon` and a `commute_lat`/`commute_lon` isochrone are three ways of drawing the SAME
thing  -  one search area  -  so no two of them can be combined (400).

**Commute is the one exception**, and it is a trap upstream: a free-text `location` is silently IGNORED
when a commute origin is set, so `location=Round Rock, TX` with an Austin commute origin would hand back
Austin homes with no warning. This API rejects that combination with a 400  -  use `city` + `state_code`
(or `postal_code`) instead, which correctly intersects with the isochrone.

city.description:
**City name** to search in. Use it together with `state_code`  -  a city name on its own is
ambiguous (there are Austins in TX, MN and IN).

Examples: `Austin`, `Miami`, `New York`, `Los Angeles`.

Ignored when the free-text `location` parameter is set.

state_code.description:
**2-letter US state code.** Pairs with `city`, `county` or `neighborhood`.

Examples: `TX` (Texas), `CA` (California), `NY` (New York), `FL` (Florida), `AZ` (Arizona).

Case-insensitive  -  `tx` and `TX` behave identically. Ignored when `location` is set.

postal_code.description:
**5-digit US ZIP code.** The most precise structured location filter  -  no `state_code` needed.

Examples: `78701` (downtown Austin), `10027` (Harlem, NYC), `33139` (Miami Beach).

Ignored when `location` is set.

county.description:
**County name**, without the word "County". Pair it with `state_code`.

Examples: `Travis` (Austin), `Miami-Dade`, `Los Angeles`, `Maricopa`.

Ignored when `location` is set.

neighborhood.description:
**Neighborhood name.** Pair it with `city` + `state_code`, since neighborhood names repeat
across metros.

Examples: `Downtown`, `East Austin`, `Harlem`, `South Beach`.

Ignored when `location` is set. Free-text `location` usually resolves neighborhoods more
reliably (`Harlem, New York, NY`).

lat.description:
**Latitude of the radius-search centre point** (decimal degrees, WGS84).

Must be sent together with `lon`; the pair defines the centre of a `radius_miles` circle.

- `30.2672`  -  Austin, TX
- `40.7128`  -  New York, NY
- `25.7617`  -  Miami, FL

Range `-90` to `90`. Verified: every one of 30 sampled results fell inside the requested radius.

**Precedence:** free-text `location` overrides `city` / `state_code` / `postal_code` / `county` /
`neighborhood`  -  send one style or the other, not both.

A search AREA (`lat`+`lon` radius, or `polygon`) **intersects** with whatever location you also pass  - 
it does not replace it. A 5-mile downtown-Austin radius returns 2,693 homes alone, 2,661 with
`location=Austin, TX`, and **0** with `location=Round Rock, TX`  -  correctly zero, because that radius
reaches no Round Rock homes. So only add a location to a radius/polygon search when you genuinely want
both constraints.

`lat`/`lon`, `polygon` and a `commute_lat`/`commute_lon` isochrone are three ways of drawing the SAME
thing  -  one search area  -  so no two of them can be combined (400).

**Commute is the one exception**, and it is a trap upstream: a free-text `location` is silently IGNORED
when a commute origin is set, so `location=Round Rock, TX` with an Austin commute origin would hand back
Austin homes with no warning. This API rejects that combination with a 400  -  use `city` + `state_code`
(or `postal_code`) instead, which correctly intersects with the isochrone.

lon.description:
**Longitude of the radius-search centre point** (decimal degrees, WGS84).

Must be sent together with `lat`. US longitudes are NEGATIVE  -  a positive value puts the centre in
Asia and returns 0 results.

- `-97.7431`  -  Austin, TX
- `-74.0060`  -  New York, NY
- `-80.1918`  -  Miami, FL

Range `-180` to `180`.

radius_miles.description:
**Search radius in miles** around the `lat` / `lon` centre point.

Default `5` when omitted. Maximum `50`  -  a larger radius is rejected upstream.

How much a radius widens the result set (Austin, TX centre `30.2672,-97.7431`, `for_sale`):
- `1`  -  326 homes
- `2`  -  977 homes
- `5`  -  2,762 homes
- `10`  -  5,383 homes
- `25`  -  18,410 homes
- `50`  -  37,421 homes (the cap)

Ignored unless BOTH `lat` and `lon` are supplied.

commute_lat.description:
**Latitude of the commute origin**  -  the place you want to travel FROM, typically a workplace or a
school. Homes are then filtered to whatever is reachable from it inside `commute_minutes`.

Required together with `commute_lon`: one without the other returns a 400.

- `30.2672`  -  downtown Austin, TX
- `40.7128`  -  Lower Manhattan, New York, NY
- `25.7617`  -  downtown Miami, FL

Range `-90` to `90`.

**Mutually exclusive with the `lat` / `lon` / `radius_miles` radius search and with `polygon`**  -  the
isochrone IS the search area, and upstream accepts exactly one. Sending a commute together with either
of them returns a 400.

**On its own, the isochrone is not bounded by any city.** A 60-minute drive out of downtown Austin
spills well past the city limits, so it can return MORE homes than Austin itself has: 14,309 reachable
for-sale listings against an Austin baseline of 7,425. That is correct  -  the extra homes are in
Round Rock, Kyle, Georgetown and the rest of the metro.

**Adding a location INTERSECTS with the isochrone**, it does not widen it. The same 30-minute drive
returns 6,261 homes on its own but 5,600 when combined with `location=Austin, TX`  -  you get only the
homes that are both inside Austin and inside the travel-time band. Leave the location off when you want
"anywhere I can reach in N minutes"; add one when you want "inside this city AND reachable in N minutes".

`/search-by-commute` is the dedicated endpoint for this filter and requires the pair up front.

commute_lon.description:
**Longitude of the commute origin**  -  the place you want to travel FROM.

Required together with `commute_lat`. US longitudes are NEGATIVE  -  a positive value puts the origin in
Asia and returns 0 results.

- `-97.7431`  -  downtown Austin, TX
- `-74.0060`  -  Lower Manhattan, New York, NY
- `-80.1918`  -  downtown Miami, FL

Range `-180` to `180`.

**Mutually exclusive with the `lat` / `lon` / `radius_miles` radius search and with `polygon`**  -  the
isochrone IS the search area, and upstream accepts exactly one. Sending a commute together with either
of them returns a 400.

commute_minutes.description:
**Travel-time budget for the commute isochrone, in minutes.** Default: `30` when omitted.

A CLOSED set of six values  -  anything else (`15`, `45`, `90`, …) is rejected with a 400:

- `10`  -  10 minutes (Austin, TX by car: 2,258 for-sale homes)
- `20`  -  20 minutes
- `30`  -  30 minutes, the default (Austin, TX by car: 6,262 · on foot: 1,777)
- `40`  -  40 minutes
- `50`  -  50 minutes
- `60`  -  60 minutes (Austin, TX by car: 14,310  -  nearly double the 7,426-listing Austin
  baseline, because an hour of driving leaves the city entirely)

Ignored unless BOTH `commute_lat` and `commute_lon` are supplied.

commute_transport.description:
**How the commute is travelled.** Default: `drive` when omitted.

- `drive`  -  by car (default). Austin, TX 30-minute isochrone: 6,262 for-sale homes
- `walk`  -  on foot. Austin, TX 30-minute isochrone: 1,777 for-sale homes

**Only these two modes actually work.** `cycle` and `public_transport` exist in the upstream
enum but are **unwired**: they are accepted and then silently ignored, returning the FULL
unfiltered result set as though no commute filter had been applied (verified  -  Austin for-sale
returns the same 7,425 at every interval, byte-identical to sending no commute at all).

This API rejects them with a 400 rather than pass that through, because a silently-unfiltered
page of results is far more damaging than an error: you would believe you were seeing homes
within a 30-minute bike ride and actually be seeing the whole metro.

Ignored unless BOTH `commute_lat` and `commute_lon` are supplied.

status.description:
**Listing lifecycle bucket.** Defaults to `for_sale` when omitted.

- `for_sale`  -  active for-sale listings (Austin, TX: 7,593)
- `for_rent`  -  active rentals (Austin, TX: 7,283)
- `sold`  -  closed sales (Austin, TX: 126,013)
- `ready_to_build`  -  builder plans / buildable lots
- `off_market`  -  no longer actively listed
- `other`  -  everything else Realtor.com tracks

Validated upstream: an unknown token returns a 400 listing the valid values.

**Tip:** `/properties-for-sale`, `/properties-for-rent` and `/properties-sold` pin this for you,
so you never have to send it there.

For the finer-grained status the listing agent set in the MLS itself  -  Active vs Pending vs Sold  - 
use `mls_status`.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

mls_status.description:
**Status the listing agent set in the source MLS**  -  a finer signal than `status`.

`status` is the Realtor.com lifecycle bucket (`for_sale`, `sold`, …); `mls_status` is what the
MLS itself reports, so it separates a genuinely available home from one already under contract
*inside the same bucket*.

**Case-sensitive.** The tokens are capitalised exactly as shown  -  lower-case `active` is
rejected. Counts are live Austin, TX matches:

- `Active`  -  on the market and taking offers (6,522 of the 7,593 `for_sale` listings)
- `Pending`  -  accepted offer, under contract (568 of the same 7,593)
- `Sold`  -  closed sale (92,033 of the 126,013 `sold` records  -  pair it with `status=sold`)

This is a CLOSED set of three: anything else hard-errors upstream and comes back as a 400.

Examples: `mls_status=Active` (skip everything under contract), `mls_status=Active,Pending`,
`status=sold&mls_status=Sold`.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

property_type.description:
**Primary property-type filter.**

- `single_family`  -  single-family houses
- `condos`  -  condominiums
- `townhomes`  -  townhouses / rowhouses
- `multi_family`  -  duplexes, triplexes and small apartment buildings
- `mobile`  -  mobile / manufactured homes
- `land`  -  land and vacant lots
- `farm`  -  farms and ranches
- `condo_townhome_rowhome_coop`  -  the combined condo/townhome/rowhome/co-op bucket
- `apartment`  -  apartment units (New York, NY: 121)
- `coop`  -  housing co-operatives (New York, NY: 8,193)
- `condop`  -  cond-ops, the NYC condo/co-op hybrid (New York, NY: 78)
- `duplex_triplex`  -  duplex / triplex (Los Angeles, CA: 3)
- `other`  -  anything else (New York, NY: 2)

**Not valid:** `townhouse` (the real token is `townhomes`) and `commercial` (accepted upstream but
returns 0 in every market). Unknown tokens return a 400 listing the valid values.

Full token list: `single_family`, `condos`, `townhomes`, `multi_family`, `mobile`, `land`, `farm`, `condo_townhome_rowhome_coop`, `apartment`, `coop`, `condop`, `duplex_triplex`, `other`.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

sub_type.description:
**Finer-grained property sub-type**, applied on top of `property_type`.

A CLOSED set of exactly three tokens  -  anything outside it hard-errors upstream and comes back
as a 400 (this is stricter than `exterior_styles`, which silently returns 0):

- `condo`  -  condominium (1,776 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings)
- `townhouse`  -  townhouse / rowhouse (147 in Austin, TX). Note the SINGULAR spelling here; the
  equivalent `property_type` token is the plural `townhomes`.
- `co_op`  -  housing co-operative. Overwhelmingly a New York phenomenon: 7,671 in New York, NY
  against 0 in Austin, TX. An empty result outside NYC is correct, not an error.

Examples: `sub_type=condo`, `sub_type=condo,townhouse`, `sub_type=co_op` (with a NYC location).

Verified as a true OR union: `condo` and `townhouse` together return exactly the sum of the two
sent on their own.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

exclude_type.description:
**Property types to EXCLUDE**  -  the inverse of `property_type`. Takes the same vocabulary.

Verified: `exclude_type=land` leaves 7,043 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings.

Useful when you want "everything except" one bucket, e.g. `exclude_type=land,mobile`, instead of
listing the ten types you do want. Unknown tokens return a 400 listing the valid values.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

exterior_styles.description:
**Architectural style** of the home.

- `ranch`  -  verified live, but rare: only 1 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings

This is an OPEN vocabulary that upstream does NOT validate  -  an unrecognised style silently
returns 0 results, and even valid styles are populated on very few listings. Treat it as a
best-effort filter.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

home_type.description:
**Listing KIND**  -  not the property type. Describes whether the home physically exists yet.

- `home`  -  a real, built home (the vast majority of listings)
- `plan`  -  a builder floor plan; the home is not built yet
- `spec_home`  -  a completed builder inventory home

Validated upstream: an unknown token returns a 400 listing the valid values.

**Shortcut:** `hide_homes_not_yet_built=true` drops `plan` listings without you having to spell
out the other two kinds. Sending both is rejected with a 400.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

heating_cooling.description:
**Heating / cooling systems** the home must have.

Every value is validated (an unknown token returns a 400 listing the valid values). Counts are
the Austin, TX for-sale matches out of 7,593:

- `central_air`  -  Central Air (6,283)
- `central_heat`  -  Central Heat (5,832)
- `forced_air`  -  Forced Air (125)
- `energy_efficient`  -  Energy Efficient (1,192)

Example: `heating_cooling=central_air,central_heat`.

Multiple values allowed, but they are combined with **AND**  -  a listing must have EVERY value listed, so each extra value NARROWS the result set. (Verified in Austin, TX: `swimming_pool` alone ~1,100 listings, `fireplace` alone ~3,000, both together 696.) Comma-separated.

home_features.description:
**Interior and structural features** the home must have.

Every value is validated (an unknown token returns a 400 listing the valid values). Counts are
the Austin, TX for-sale matches out of 7,593:

- `basement`  -  Basement (61)
- `den_or_office`  -  Den / Office (69)
- `dining_room`  -  Dining Room (1,191)
- `family_room`  -  Family Room (559)
- `game_room`  -  Game Room (760)
- `washer_dryer`  -  In-home Laundry (1,854)
- `disability_features`  -  Accessibility Features (0 in Austin  -  rare everywhere)
- `fireplace`  -  Fireplace (3,034)
- `hardwood_floors`  -  Hardwood Floors (3,439)
- `horse_facilities`  -  Horse Facilities (7)
- `spa_or_hot_tub`  -  Spa / Hot Tub (338)
- `swimming_pool`  -  Swimming Pool (1,105)
- `tennis_court`  -  Tennis Court (255)
- `single_story`  -  Single Story (3,338)
- `two_or_more_stories`  -  Multi-Story (3,664)
- `lease_option`  -  Lease Option (8)
- `pets_allowed`  -  Pets Allowed (123)

Example: `home_features=fireplace,hardwood_floors`.

Multiple values allowed, but they are combined with **AND**  -  a listing must have EVERY value listed, so each extra value NARROWS the result set. (Verified in Austin, TX: `swimming_pool` alone ~1,100 listings, `fireplace` alone ~3,000, both together 696.) Comma-separated.

lot_features.description:
**Lot position and view** features.

Every value is validated (an unknown token returns a 400 listing the valid values). Counts are
the Austin, TX for-sale matches out of 7,593:

- `corner_lot`  -  Corner Lot (850)
- `cul_de_sac`  -  Cul de Sac (585)
- `golf_course_lot_or_frontage`  -  Golf Course Lot (1)
- `waterfront`  -  Waterfront (347)
- `city_view`  -  City View (713)
- `golf_course_view`  -  Golf Course View (76)
- `hill_or_mountain_view`  -  Hill / Mountain View (14)
- `lake_view`  -  Lake View (459)
- `ocean_view`  -  Ocean View (46 in Austin; 2,228 in Miami, FL)
- `river_view`  -  River View (150)
- `water_view`  -  Water View (871)
- `view`  -  View of any kind (3,877)

Example: `lot_features=waterfront,water_view`.

Multiple values allowed, but they are combined with **AND**  -  a listing must have EVERY value listed, so each extra value NARROWS the result set. (Verified in Austin, TX: `swimming_pool` alone ~1,100 listings, `fireplace` alone ~3,000, both together 696.) Comma-separated.

community_features.description:
**Shared / community amenities** (HOA and subdivision level).

Every value is validated (an unknown token returns a 400 listing the valid values). Counts are
the Austin, TX for-sale matches out of 7,593:

- `community_swimming_pool`  -  Swimming Pool (2,829)
- `community_boat_facilities`  -  Boat Facilities (7)
- `community_spa_or_hot_tub`  -  Spa / Hot Tub (139)
- `community_tennis_court`  -  Tennis Court(s) (595)
- `community_golf`  -  Golf (391)
- `community_clubhouse`  -  Clubhouse (1,118)
- `community_security_features`  -  Security Features (4,162)
- `senior_community`  -  Senior (55+) Community (0 in Austin; 18 in Scottsdale, AZ)
- `community_horse_facilities`  -  Horse Facilities (2)
- `community_park`  -  Park (2,533)
- `recreation_facilities`  -  Recreation Facilities (3,616)

Example: `community_features=community_swimming_pool,community_clubhouse`.

Multiple values allowed, but they are combined with **AND**  -  a listing must have EVERY value listed, so each extra value NARROWS the result set. (Verified in Austin, TX: `swimming_pool` alone ~1,100 listings, `fireplace` alone ~3,000, both together 696.) Comma-separated.

nyc_amenities.description:
**Dense-urban building amenities.** Named for New York City, where they are populated on most
listings, but they work in any market.

Every value is validated (an unknown token returns a 400 listing the valid values):

- `community_doorman`  -  Doorman (0 in Austin, TX; 7,730 in New York, NY)
- `community_elevator`  -  Elevator (0 in Austin, TX; 10,648 in New York, NY)
- `dishwasher`  -  Dishwasher (5,557 of 7,593 in Austin, TX)
- `community_outdoor_space`  -  Outdoor Space (5,805 in Austin, TX; 4,775 in New York, NY)

Example: `nyc_amenities=community_doorman,community_elevator,dishwasher`.

Multiple values allowed, but they are combined with **AND**  -  a listing must have EVERY value listed, so each extra value NARROWS the result set. (Verified in Austin, TX: `swimming_pool` alone ~1,100 listings, `fireplace` alone ~3,000, both together 696.) Comma-separated.

tags.description:
**Raw feature tags**, merged straight into the upstream tag filter.

**Warning  -  this is an OPEN vocabulary that is NOT validated upstream.** A typo or an
unrecognised tag does not raise an error: it silently returns **0 results**. (`zzz_not_a_tag`
returns 0, not a 400.)

**Use the five validated group parameters instead**  -  every token they accept is verified live,
and a bad one gets a helpful 400:
- `heating_cooling`  -  Central Air, Central Heat, Forced Air, Energy Efficient
- `home_features`  -  Fireplace, Hardwood Floors, Swimming Pool, Basement, …
- `lot_features`  -  Waterfront, Corner Lot, Cul de Sac, Lake View, …
- `community_features`  -  Community Pool, Clubhouse, Golf, Security, …
- `nyc_amenities`  -  Doorman, Elevator, Dishwasher, Outdoor Space

All five groups plus `tags` merge into ONE upstream tag array (union, de-duplicated), so they can
be mixed freely in a single request.

Only reach for `tags` when you need a tag you have actually seen in a `/search` response  -  every
result echoes its own `tags` array. Examples: `central_air`, `fireplace`, `swimming_pool`, `view`.

Multiple values allowed, but they are combined with **AND**  -  a listing must have EVERY value listed, so each extra value NARROWS the result set. (Verified in Austin, TX: `swimming_pool` alone ~1,100 listings, `fireplace` alone ~3,000, both together 696.) Comma-separated.

keywords.description:
**Free-text keyword filter** matched by Realtor.com against the listing text (agent remarks,
descriptions), not against a fixed vocabulary.

Examples: `pool`, `casita`, `guest house`, `adu`, `renovated`.

Keywords depend on how an agent wrote the listing, so they are far less reliable than the five
feature-tag groups. Use them for concepts Realtor.com has no tag for.

Multiple values allowed, but they are combined with **AND**  -  a listing must have EVERY value listed, so each extra value NARROWS the result set. (Verified in Austin, TX: `swimming_pool` alone ~1,100 listings, `fireplace` alone ~3,000, both together 696.) Comma-separated.

beds_min.description:
**Minimum number of bedrooms.**

- `1`  -  1+ bedroom
- `3`  -  3+ bedrooms (the most common family filter)
- `5`  -  5+ bedrooms

Send `beds_min` alone for "at least", `beds_max` alone for "at most", or both for a window
(`beds_min=3&beds_max=4`).

beds_max.description:
**Maximum number of bedrooms.**

- `2`  -  studios, 1-bed and 2-bed homes only
- `4`  -  up to 4 bedrooms

Pairs with `beds_min` to form a window.

baths_min.description:
**Minimum number of bathrooms.**

- `1`  -  1+ bathroom
- `2`  -  2+ bathrooms
- `3`  -  3+ bathrooms

Pairs with `baths_max` to form a window.

baths_max.description:
**Maximum number of bathrooms.**

- `2`  -  up to 2 bathrooms
- `3`  -  up to 3 bathrooms

Pairs with `baths_min` to form a window.

sqft_min.description:
**Minimum living area, in square feet** (the house itself, not the lot  -  that is `lot_sqft_min`).

Some example values:
- `500`  -  500 sqft
- `750`  -  750 sqft
- `1000`  -  1,000 sqft
- `1500`  -  1,500 sqft
- `2000`  -  2,000 sqft
- `3000`  -  3,000 sqft

Send `sqft_min` alone for "at least", `sqft_max` alone for "at most", or both for a window
(`sqft_min=1000&sqft_max=2000`).

sqft_max.description:
**Maximum living area, in square feet.**

Some example values:
- `1000`  -  1,000 sqft
- `1500`  -  1,500 sqft
- `2500`  -  2,500 sqft
- `4000`  -  4,000 sqft

Pairs with `sqft_min` to form a window.

lot_sqft_min.description:
**Minimum lot size, in square feet.** Note the unit: square feet, not acres.

Some example values:
- `2000`  -  2,000 sqft
- `10890`  -  0.25 acre
- `21780`  -  0.5 acre
- `43560`  -  1 acre
- `87120`  -  2 acres
- `217800`  -  5 acres

Send `lot_sqft_min` alone for "at least", `lot_sqft_max` alone for "at most", or both for a window
(`lot_sqft_min=10890&lot_sqft_max=43560`).

lot_sqft_max.description:
**Maximum lot size, in square feet.**

Some example values:
- `7500`  -  7,500 sqft
- `10890`  -  0.25 acre
- `21780`  -  0.5 acre
- `43560`  -  1 acre

Pairs with `lot_sqft_min` to form a window.

price_min.description:
**Minimum price, in whole US dollars** (no commas, no `$`).

Some example values:
- `250000`  -  $250,000
- `500000`  -  $500,000
- `1000000`  -  $1,000,000

On `for_rent` searches this is the MONTHLY rent (e.g. `1500` = $1,500/month).

For closed sales use `sold_price_min` instead  -  `price_min` filters the list price.

price_max.description:
**Maximum price, in whole US dollars** (no commas, no `$`).

Some example values:
- `350000`  -  $350,000
- `750000`  -  $750,000
- `2000000`  -  $2,000,000

On `for_rent` searches this is the MONTHLY rent (e.g. `3000` = $3,000/month).

Pairs with `price_min` to form a window.

year_built_min.description:
**Earliest year the home was built**  -  i.e. "no older than this".

- `2000`  -  built in 2000 or later
- `2020`  -  built in 2020 or later

`home_age_max` expresses the same thing in years instead of a calendar year; send one or the other,
not both (a colliding pair returns a 400).

year_built_max.description:
**Latest year the home was built**  -  i.e. "no newer than this". Useful for historic homes.

- `1970`  -  built in 1970 or earlier
- `1999`  -  built before the 2000s

`home_age_min` expresses the same thing in years; send one or the other, not both (a colliding pair
returns a 400).

home_age_min.description:
**Minimum age of the home, in years**  -  "at least this old". Converted to a `year_built` ceiling for
you, so you never have to do the arithmetic.

Some example values:
- `3`  -  3 years
- `5`  -  5 years
- `10`  -  10 years
- `50`  -  50 years
- `100`  -  100 years

An alternative to `year_built_max`. Sending both returns a 400  -  pick one.

home_age_max.description:
**Maximum age of the home, in years**  -  "newer than this". Converted to a `year_built` floor for you.

Some example values:
- `3`  -  built within the last 3 years
- `5`  -  5 years
- `10`  -  10 years
- `20`  -  20 years

An alternative to `year_built_min`. Sending both returns a 400  -  pick one.

Pairs with `home_age_min` to form a window (`home_age_min=1&home_age_max=5`).

garage_min.description:
**Minimum number of garage spaces.**

- `1`  -  1+ car garage
- `2`  -  2+ car garage (the most common filter)
- `3`  -  3+ car garage

hoa_fee_max.description:
**Maximum monthly HOA fee, in US dollars.** Strict variant  -  it filters on the reported HOA fee.

- `100`  -  up to $100/month
- `300`  -  up to $300/month

Related: `hoa_fee_optional_max` also keeps listings with no HOA fee at all, and `no_hoa_fee=true`
returns only homes with no HOA.

hoa_fee_optional_max.description:
**Maximum monthly HOA fee, in US dollars  -  but listings with NO HOA fee still qualify.**

This is the "optional HOA" variant most home shoppers actually want: a fee ceiling that does not
accidentally exclude every HOA-free house.

Verified: `hoa_fee_optional_max=100` returns 5,297 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings.

Use `hoa_fee_max` for the strict version.

monthly_payment_max.description:
**Maximum estimated total monthly payment, in US dollars**  -  the Realtor.com estimate that bundles
principal, interest, taxes and insurance, not just the mortgage.

- `2000`  -  up to $2,000/month
- `3500`  -  up to $3,500/month

Handy when a customer thinks in budget rather than list price.

days_on_market_min.description:
**Minimum days on market**  -  "has been listed at least this long".

- `30`  -  on the market a month or more
- `90`  -  stale listings, often the most negotiable

An alternative way to express `list_date_max`.

days_on_market_max.description:
**Maximum days on market**  -  "listed within the last N days". The fastest way to poll for new
inventory.

- `1`  -  listed today or yesterday
- `7`  -  listed in the last week
- `30`  -  listed in the last month

An alternative way to express `list_date_min`. Combine with `sort=newest` to get the freshest
listings first.

new_construction.description:
**Only new-construction listings.** Default: unset (no filter).

Verified: `true` returns 1,130 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings.

This flag only NARROWS when `true`. To do the opposite, use `hide_new_construction=true`.

(Equivalent to a competitor `newConstructionOnly` parameter.)

hide_new_construction.description:
**Exclude new construction**  -  a genuine inverse, not just the absence of `new_construction`.

Verified: `true` returns 6,457 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings (7,593 − 1,130 + overlap).

Default: unset. Do not send this together with `new_construction=true`  -  they cancel out to 0.

hide_homes_not_yet_built.description:
**Exclude homes that are not built yet**  -  drops Realtor.com `plan` listings (builder floor plans),
keeping real homes (`home`) and completed builder inventory (`spec_home`).

Default: `false` (floor plans are included).

A shortcut for setting `home_type` by hand; sending both returns a 400. Has no effect in markets
with no floor-plan listings.

(Equivalent to a competitor `hideHomesNotYetBuilt` parameter.)

foreclosure.description:
**Only foreclosure listings.** Default: unset (no filter).

Verified: `true` returns roughly 59 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings  -  foreclosures are a
small slice of any healthy market.

This flag only NARROWS when `true`. To do the opposite, use `hide_foreclosures=true`.

(Equivalent to a competitor `foreclosuresOnly` parameter.)

hide_foreclosures.description:
**Exclude foreclosure listings**  -  a genuine inverse, not just the absence of `foreclosure`.

Verified: `true` returns 7,529 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings.

Default: unset. Do not send this together with `foreclosure=true`  -  they cancel out to 0.

(Equivalent to a competitor `hideForeclosures` parameter.)

pending.description:
**Only listings with a pending sale** (under contract, no contingencies left). Default: unset.

Only narrows when `true`. See `pending_or_contingent_only` for pending + contingent together, and
`hide_pending_contingent` to remove both.

contingent.description:
**Only listings under a contract contingency** (accepted offer, still subject to conditions).
Default: unset.

Only narrows when `true`. See `pending_or_contingent_only` and `hide_pending_contingent`.

pending_or_contingent_only.description:
**Only pending OR contingent listings**  -  everything already under contract, in one flag.

Verified: `true` returns 1,349 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings.

Default: unset. The exact inverse of `hide_pending_contingent`; never send both.

hide_pending_contingent.description:
**Exclude pending and contingent listings**  -  leaves only homes genuinely still available. A genuine
inverse, not just the absence of the flags above.

Verified: `true` returns 6,243 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings.

Default: `false`. The single most useful flag for buyer-facing apps.

(Equivalent to a competitor `hidePendingContingent` parameter.)

short_sale.description:
**Only short-sale listings** (seller owes more than the sale price; lender approval required).

Default: unset. Only narrows when `true`.

auction.description:
**Only homes being sold at auction.** Default: unset. Only narrows when `true`.

Auction inventory is very thin  -  7 of 7,548 Austin for-sale listings  -  so expect small result sets
and pair it with a wide location rather than a narrow one.

Distinct from `foreclosure`: a foreclosure is a bank-owned/distressed listing, which may or may not
be auctioned. Use `foreclosure` for distressed inventory generally.

senior_community.description:
**Only 55+ / age-restricted communities.** Default: unset.

Verified: 0 matches in Austin, TX, but 18 in Scottsdale, AZ  -  this filter is only meaningful in
retirement markets (AZ, FL, NV, parts of CA).

Equivalent to passing `senior_community` inside `community_features`.

(Equivalent to a competitor `seniorCommunityOnly` parameter.)

has_open_house.description:
**Only listings with an upcoming open house.** Default: unset.

For a specific date window use `open_house_date_min` / `open_house_date_max` instead.

has_virtual_tour.description:
**Only listings with a virtual (online) tour.** Default: unset. Only narrows when `true`.

Verified: ~2,400 of ~7,550 Austin for-sale listings  -  roughly a third of inventory.

Related flags, narrowest to broadest: `matterport` (a Matterport 3D walkthrough specifically, ~570)
⊂ `has_virtual_tour` (any online tour, ~2,400) ⊂ `has_tour` (any tour incl. in-person, ~3,000).
The listing payload carries the tour links in `virtual_tours[]`.

has_tour.description:
**Only listings with any tour**  -  virtual or in-person. Broader than `has_virtual_tour`.

Default: unset. Only narrows when `true`.

matterport.description:
**Only listings with a Matterport 3D walkthrough.** Default: unset.

Narrower than `has_virtual_tour`, which also counts video and photo tours.

has_photos.description:
**Only listings that have photos.** Default: unset.

Verified: `true` returns 7,578 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings  -  almost every listing has
photos, so this barely narrows anything. Use it to drop the handful of photo-less records.

has_video.description:
**Only listings with a video tour.** Default: unset.

Verified as a valid filter, but video is rare: Austin, TX returned 0 matches. Expect small or empty
result sets in most markets  -  an empty response here is correct, not an error.

has_specials.description:
**Only listings advertising a special or concession** (move-in specials, free rent, seller credits).
Mostly a rental concept.

Default: unset. Verified as a valid filter, but Austin, TX for-sale returned 0  -  expect this to bite
mainly on `for_rent` searches.

no_hoa_fee.description:
**Only homes with no HOA fee at all.** Default: unset.

Stricter than `hoa_fee_max`. If you want a fee ceiling that still keeps HOA-free homes, use
`hoa_fee_optional_max`.

boundary.description:
**Include the map boundary polygon in the response.** Default: `false`.

When `true`, the response gains a `boundary` field containing the GeoJSON polygon of the searched
area (city, ZIP, neighborhood, …) so you can draw it on a map.

For the polygon on its own  -  without paging through listings  -  call `/map-boundary`.

elementary_rating_min.description:
**Minimum GreatSchools rating (1-10) for the assigned elementary school.**

- `5`  -  average or better
- `7`  -  above average
- `9`  -  top-rated only

Applies to the elementary school assigned to the listing address.

middle_rating_min.description:
**Minimum GreatSchools rating (1-10) for the assigned middle school.**

- `5`  -  average or better
- `7`  -  above average
- `9`  -  top-rated only

high_rating_min.description:
**Minimum GreatSchools rating (1-10) for the assigned high school.**

- `5`  -  average or better
- `7`  -  above average
- `9`  -  top-rated only

has_private_school.description:
**Only listings with a private school among their nearby / assigned schools.** Default: unset.

Verified: `true` returns 7,186 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings  -  in a metro area nearly
every address has a private school nearby, so this barely narrows the set.

flood_risk.description:
**Flood risk tier** for the home, from the First Street environmental model.

- `minimal`  -  low risk
- `moderate`  -  medium risk
- `severe`  -  high risk

Flood risk blends FEMA zone data with First Street flood modelling.

**Important:** this filters to listings AT the chosen tier, NOT "at most" that tier. To find
low-risk homes, pass `minimal`.

The five risk filters (`flood_risk`, `fire_risk`, `heat_risk`, `wind_risk`, `air_risk`) combine
into a single upstream filter, so they can be sent together.

fire_risk.description:
**Wildfire risk tier** for the home, from the First Street environmental model.

- `minimal`  -  low risk
- `moderate`  -  medium risk
- `severe`  -  high risk

Wildfire risk is driven by vegetation, slope and historical fire activity.

**Important:** this filters to listings AT the chosen tier, NOT "at most" that tier. To find
low-risk homes, pass `minimal`.

The five risk filters (`flood_risk`, `fire_risk`, `heat_risk`, `wind_risk`, `air_risk`) combine
into a single upstream filter, so they can be sent together.

heat_risk.description:
**Heat risk tier** for the home, from the First Street environmental model.

- `minimal`  -  low risk
- `moderate`  -  medium risk
- `severe`  -  high risk

Heat risk reflects projected extreme-temperature days.

**Important:** this filters to listings AT the chosen tier, NOT "at most" that tier. To find
low-risk homes, pass `minimal`.

The five risk filters (`flood_risk`, `fire_risk`, `heat_risk`, `wind_risk`, `air_risk`) combine
into a single upstream filter, so they can be sent together.

wind_risk.description:
**Wind risk tier** for the home, from the First Street environmental model.

- `minimal`  -  low risk
- `moderate`  -  medium risk
- `severe`  -  high risk

Wind risk reflects hurricane and severe-storm exposure.

**Important:** this filters to listings AT the chosen tier, NOT "at most" that tier. To find
low-risk homes, pass `minimal`.

The five risk filters (`flood_risk`, `fire_risk`, `heat_risk`, `wind_risk`, `air_risk`) combine
into a single upstream filter, so they can be sent together.

air_risk.description:
**Air quality risk tier** for the home, from the First Street environmental model.

- `minimal`  -  low risk
- `moderate`  -  medium risk
- `severe`  -  high risk

Air risk reflects the projected number of poor-air-quality days.

**Important:** this filters to listings AT the chosen tier, NOT "at most" that tier. To find
low-risk homes, pass `minimal`.

The five risk filters (`flood_risk`, `fire_risk`, `heat_risk`, `wind_risk`, `air_risk`) combine
into a single upstream filter, so they can be sent together.

list_date_min.description:
**Listed on or after this date**  -  the freshest-inventory filter.

Format: `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-07-01`). `07/01/2026` and `2026/07/01` are rejected with a 400.

Verified: `list_date_min=2026-07-01` returned 1,853 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings.

`days_on_market_max` expresses the same idea as a rolling window.

list_date_max.description:
**Listed on or before this date**  -  finds long-sitting inventory, which is often the most
negotiable.

Format: `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-07-01`). `07/01/2026` and `2026/07/01` are rejected with a 400.

Verified: `list_date_max=2025-01-01` returned 142 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings.

Pairs with `list_date_min` to form a window. `days_on_market_min` expresses the same idea in days.

price_reduced_date_min.description:
**Price was reduced on or after this date**  -  motivated sellers.

Format: `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-07-01`). `07/01/2026` and `2026/07/01` are rejected with a 400.

Verified: `price_reduced_date_min=2026-07-01` returned 2,054 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale
listings.

open_house_date_min.description:
**Has an open house on or after this date.**

Format: `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-07-01`). `07/01/2026` and `2026/07/01` are rejected with a 400.

Verified: `open_house_date_min=2026-07-30` returned 271 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings.

Pair it with `open_house_date_max` to search a weekend window.

open_house_date_max.description:
**Has an open house on or before this date.**

Format: `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-07-01`). `07/01/2026` and `2026/07/01` are rejected with a 400.

Verified as a window: `open_house_date_min=2026-07-30` + `open_house_date_max=2026-08-03` returned
264 of the 7,593 Austin, TX for-sale listings.

For "any upcoming open house", `has_open_house=true` is simpler.

mls_id.description:
**MLS number**  -  the id printed on the listing sheet and on the Realtor.com detail page.

Exact match only: a prefix or partial MLS number is rejected upstream, so send the whole thing.

Verified: `mls_id=3202671` returns exactly 1 listing.

Combine it with a `location` to disambiguate  -  MLS numbers are unique per MLS, not nationally.

listing_id.description:
**Realtor.com internal listing id**  -  the `listing_id` field echoed on every search result.

Exact match only. Verified: `listing_id=2993201291` returns exactly 1 listing.

Different from `property_id`: a property can be listed many times over the years, so a
`listing_id` pins one specific listing while `property_id` pins the address.

exclude_property_ids.description:
**Property ids to omit from the results.** Takes the `property_id` values from any search
response.

Example: `exclude_property_ids=9683615082,9612291762`.

Useful for de-duplicating across pages, or for hiding listings a user has already dismissed.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

selling_agent_name.description:
**Full name of the agent on the SELLING side of the transaction.**

**Exact, whole-name match**  -  there is no partial, prefix or fuzzy matching. `Guadalupe` does not
find `Guadalupe Abbud`; spell the name exactly as Realtor.com holds it, including middle initials
and suffixes.

Verified: `selling_agent_name=Guadalupe Abbud` returns 3 listings.

Get the exact spelling from `/agents-search`, or from the `advertisers[]` block of any property
detail. A name that matches nobody returns 0 results, not an error  -  so an empty response usually
means the spelling is off.

**Prefer `fulfillment_id` whenever you have it:** an advertiser id is stable and unambiguous,
while two agents can share a name and the same agent can be spelled differently across MLSs.

fulfillment_id.description:
**Realtor.com advertiser id of an agent**  -  the cleanest way to pull one agent's entire book of
business.

Unlike `selling_agent_name`, this works on EVERY status. Verified for agent `3809719`:

- `status=for_sale`  -  70 listings
- `status=for_rent`  -  10 listings
- `status=sold`  -  383 listings
- `status=off_market`  -  9 listings

Where to get one:

- `/agents-search`  -  every agent row echoes its own `fulfillment_id`
- any property detail  -  `advertisers[].fulfillment_id`

Examples: `fulfillment_id=3809719` (one agent), `fulfillment_id=3809719,1715146` (a whole team in a
single call).

An id that matches no listings returns 0 results rather than a 400  -  it is not validated against the
agent directory. `/agent-listings` is the dedicated endpoint for this filter.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

sold_date_min.description:
**Closed on or after this date.** Applies to sold listings only (`status=sold`, which
`/properties-sold` sets for you).

Format: `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-07-01`). `07/01/2026` and `2026/07/01` are rejected with a 400.

Verified: `sold_date_min=2026-06-01` returned 2,282 of the 126,013 Austin, TX sold records.

sold_date_max.description:
**Closed on or before this date.** Applies to sold listings only (`status=sold`).

Format: `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-07-01`). `07/01/2026` and `2026/07/01` are rejected with a 400.

Pairs with `sold_date_min` to bracket a month, quarter or year of closed sales.

sold_price_min.description:
**Minimum closed sale price, in whole US dollars.** Applies to sold listings only (`status=sold`,
which `/properties-sold` sets for you). Filters the actual sale price, not the list price.

- `250000`  -  $250,000
- `500000`  -  $500,000

Verified: in Miami, FL, `sold_price_min=500000` returned 52,192 of 140,502 sold records.

**Non-disclosure states return 0.** Texas is the big one (also LA, MS, NM, UT, and others): state
law lets sale prices be withheld, so Realtor.com has no sold price to filter on, `last_sold_price`
comes back `null`, and any `sold_price_*` filter returns 0 results. That is correct upstream
behaviour, not a bug  -  use `sold_date_*` in those markets instead.

sold_price_max.description:
**Maximum closed sale price, in whole US dollars.** Applies to sold listings only (`status=sold`).

- `400000`  -  $400,000
- `1000000`  -  $1,000,000

Pairs with `sold_price_min` to form a window.

**Non-disclosure states return 0.** Texas is the big one (also LA, MS, NM, UT, and others): state
law lets sale prices be withheld, so `last_sold_price` is `null` and any `sold_price_*` filter
returns 0 results there. That is correct upstream behaviour, not a bug.

move_in_date_min.description:
**Earliest date the rental is available to move in** (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

Applies to rentals only (`status=for_rent`, which `/properties-for-rent` sets for you).

Format: `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-07-01`). `07/01/2026` and `2026/07/01` are rejected with a 400.

Verified: `move_in_date_min=2026-09-01` returned 816 of the 7,283 Austin, TX rental listings.

cats.description:
**Only rentals that allow cats.** Default: unset (no filter). Only narrows when `true`.

Mainly meaningful on `for_rent` searches.

dogs.description:
**Only rentals that allow dogs.** Default: unset (no filter). Only narrows when `true`.

Mainly meaningful on `for_rent` searches. Realtor.com has no size split  -  `dogs_large`,
`dogs_small` and `no_pets_allowed` are rejected upstream, so `dogs` is the only dog filter.

sort.description:
**Result ordering.** Default: `relevant` (Realtor.com relevance ranking).

- `relevant`  -  Realtor.com relevance (default)
- `newest`  -  most recently listed first
- `oldest`  -  longest on market first
- `price_low`  -  lowest price first
- `price_high`  -  highest price first
- `beds`  -  most bedrooms first
- `baths`  -  most bathrooms first
- `sqft`  -  largest living area first
- `lot_size`  -  largest lot first
- `year_built`  -  newest construction year first
- `sold_date`  -  most recently sold first (use with `status=sold`)
- `sold_price_high`  -  highest sold price first (use with `status=sold`)
- `photos`  -  most photos first
- `open_house`  -  soonest open house first

Exactly one ordering is applied: `relevant` uses the relevance ranker, any other alias uses an
explicit sort. They cannot be combined.

page.description:
**Page number, 1-indexed.** Default: `1`. Maximum: `500`.

The response echoes `page`, `page_size`, `total` and `total_pages`, so you can loop until
`page > total_pages`.

Deep paging is capped by `page * limit`; to walk a very large market, split it by ZIP, by price band
or by `lat`/`lon` radius instead of paging past the cap.

limit.description:
**Results per page.** Default: `20`. Range: `1`-`50`.

A larger `limit` means fewer round trips for the same coverage  -  `limit=50` pulls 50 listings in
one call. It has no effect on `total`, which always reports the full match count.

description: Homes currently for sale, with the full filter surface.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description:
**Free-text location  -  the simplest way to search.** Accepts anything Realtor.com autocomplete
handles, and resolves it to the right geography for you.

- `Austin, TX`  -  city + state
- `78701`  -  ZIP code
- `Travis County, TX`  -  county
- `Downtown, Austin, TX`  -  neighborhood
- `9504 Quail Village Ln, Austin, TX 78758`  -  full street address

**Precedence:** free-text `location` overrides `city` / `state_code` / `postal_code` / `county` /
`neighborhood`  -  send one style or the other, not both.

A search AREA (`lat`+`lon` radius, or `polygon`) **intersects** with whatever location you also pass  - 
it does not replace it. A 5-mile downtown-Austin radius returns 2,693 homes alone, 2,661 with
`location=Austin, TX`, and **0** with `location=Round Rock, TX`  -  correctly zero, because that radius
reaches no Round Rock homes. So only add a location to a radius/polygon search when you genuinely want
both constraints.

`lat`/`lon`, `polygon` and a `commute_lat`/`commute_lon` isochrone are three ways of drawing the SAME
thing  -  one search area  -  so no two of them can be combined (400).

**Commute is the one exception**, and it is a trap upstream: a free-text `location` is silently IGNORED
when a commute origin is set, so `location=Round Rock, TX` with an Austin commute origin would hand back
Austin homes with no warning. This API rejects that combination with a 400  -  use `city` + `state_code`
(or `postal_code`) instead, which correctly intersects with the isochrone.

- `Austin, TX`  -  city + state

- `Travis County, TX`  -  county
- `Downtown, Austin, TX`  -  neighborhood
- `9504 Quail Village Ln, Austin, TX 78758`  -  full street address

**Precedence:** free-text `location` overrides `city` / `state_code` / `postal_code` / `county` /
`neighborhood`  -  send one style or the other, not both.

A search AREA (`lat`+`lon` radius, or `polygon`) **intersects** with whatever location you also pass  - 
it does not replace it. A 5-mile downtown-Austin radius returns 2,693 homes alone, 2,661 with
`location=Austin, TX`, and **0** with `location=Round Rock, TX`  -  correctly zero, because that radius

`lat`/`lon`, `polygon` and a `commute_lat`/`commute_lon` isochrone are three ways of drawing the SAME

**Commute is the one exception**, and it is a trap upstream: a free-text `location` is silently IGNORED

parameters.name: city
parameters.description:
**City name** to search in. Use it together with `state_code`  -  a city name on its own is
ambiguous (there are Austins in TX, MN and IN).

Examples: `Austin`, `Miami`, `New York`, `Los Angeles`.

Ignored when the free-text `location` parameter is set.

schema.description:
**City name** to search in. Use it together with `state_code`  -  a city name on its own is
ambiguous (there are Austins in TX, MN and IN).

Examples: `Austin`, `Miami`, `New York`, `Los Angeles`.

Ignored when the free-text `location` parameter is set.

parameters.name: state_code
parameters.description:
**2-letter US state code.** Pairs with `city`, `county` or `neighborhood`.

Examples: `TX` (Texas), `CA` (California), `NY` (New York), `FL` (Florida), `AZ` (Arizona).

Case-insensitive  -  `tx` and `TX` behave identically. Ignored when `location` is set.

schema.description:
**2-letter US state code.** Pairs with `city`, `county` or `neighborhood`.

Examples: `TX` (Texas), `CA` (California), `NY` (New York), `FL` (Florida), `AZ` (Arizona).

Case-insensitive  -  `tx` and `TX` behave identically. Ignored when `location` is set.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description:
**5-digit US ZIP code.** The most precise structured location filter  -  no `state_code` needed.

Examples: `78701` (downtown Austin), `10027` (Harlem, NYC), `33139` (Miami Beach).

Ignored when `location` is set.

schema.description:
**5-digit US ZIP code.** The most precise structured location filter  -  no `state_code` needed.

Examples: `78701` (downtown Austin), `10027` (Harlem, NYC), `33139` (Miami Beach).

Ignored when `location` is set.

parameters.name: county
parameters.description:
**County name**, without the word "County". Pair it with `state_code`.

Examples: `Travis` (Austin), `Miami-Dade`, `Los Angeles`, `Maricopa`.

Ignored when `location` is set.

schema.description:
**County name**, without the word "County". Pair it with `state_code`.

Examples: `Travis` (Austin), `Miami-Dade`, `Los Angeles`, `Maricopa`.

Ignored when `location` is set.

parameters.name: neighborhood
parameters.description:
**Neighborhood name.** Pair it with `city` + `state_code`, since neighborhood names repeat
across metros.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description:
**Latitude of the radius-search centre point** (decimal degrees, WGS84).

Must be sent together with `lon`; the pair defines the centre of a `radius_miles` circle.

- `30.2672`  -  Austin, TX
- `40.7128`  -  New York, NY
- `25.7617`  -  Miami, FL

Range `-90` to `90`. Verified: every one of 30 sampled results fell inside the requested radius.

**Precedence:** free-text `location` overrides `city` / `state_code` / `postal_code` / `county` /
`neighborhood`  -  send one style or the other, not both.

A search AREA (`lat`+`lon` radius, or `polygon`) **intersects** with whatever location you also pass  - 
it does not replace it. A 5-mile downtown-Austin radius returns 2,693 homes alone, 2,661 with
`location=Austin, TX`, and **0** with `location=Round Rock, TX`  -  correctly zero, because that radius
reaches no Round Rock homes. So only add a location to a radius/polygon search when you genuinely want
both constraints.

`lat`/`lon`, `polygon` and a `commute_lat`/`commute_lon` isochrone are three ways of drawing the SAME
thing  -  one search area  -  so no two of them can be combined (400).

**Commute is the one exception**, and it is a trap upstream: a free-text `location` is silently IGNORED
when a commute origin is set, so `location=Round Rock, TX` with an Austin commute origin would hand back
Austin homes with no warning. This API rejects that combination with a 400  -  use `city` + `state_code`
(or `postal_code`) instead, which correctly intersects with the isochrone.

parameters.name: radius_miles

- `2`  -  977 homes
- `5`  -  2,762 homes
- `10`  -  5,383 homes
- `25`  -  18,410 homes

Ignored unless BOTH `lat` and `lon` are supplied.

parameters.name: commute_lat
parameters.description:
**Latitude of the commute origin**  -  the place you want to travel FROM, typically a workplace or a
school. Homes are then filtered to whatever is reachable from it inside `commute_minutes`.

Required together with `commute_lon`: one without the other returns a 400.

- `30.2672`  -  downtown Austin, TX
- `40.7128`  -  Lower Manhattan, New York, NY
- `25.7617`  -  downtown Miami, FL

Range `-90` to `90`.

**Mutually exclusive with the `lat` / `lon` / `radius_miles` radius search and with `polygon`**  -  the
isochrone IS the search area, and upstream accepts exactly one. Sending a commute together with either
of them returns a 400.

**On its own, the isochrone is not bounded by any city.** A 60-minute drive out of downtown Austin
spills well past the city limits, so it can return MORE homes than Austin itself has: 14,309 reachable
for-sale listings against an Austin baseline of 7,425. That is correct  -  the extra homes are in
Round Rock, Kyle, Georgetown and the rest of the metro.

**Adding a location INTERSECTS with the isochrone**, it does not widen it. The same 30-minute drive
returns 6,261 homes on its own but 5,600 when combined with `location=Austin, TX`  -  you get only the
homes that are both inside Austin and inside the travel-time band. Leave the location off when you want
"anywhere I can reach in N minutes"; add one when you want "inside this city AND reachable in N minutes".

`/search-by-commute` is the dedicated endpoint for this filter and requires the pair up front.

parameters.name: commute_minutes
parameters.description:
**Travel-time budget for the commute isochrone, in minutes.** Default: `30` when omitted.

A CLOSED set of six values  -  anything else (`15`, `45`, `90`, …) is rejected with a 400:

- `10`  -  10 minutes (Austin, TX by car: 2,258 for-sale homes)
- `20`  -  20 minutes
- `30`  -  30 minutes, the default (Austin, TX by car: 6,262 · on foot: 1,777)
- `40`  -  40 minutes
- `50`  -  50 minutes
- `60`  -  60 minutes (Austin, TX by car: 14,310  -  nearly double the 7,426-listing Austin
  baseline, because an hour of driving leaves the city entirely)

Ignored unless BOTH `commute_lat` and `commute_lon` are supplied.

parameters.name: commute_transport
parameters.description:
**How the commute is travelled.** Default: `drive` when omitted.

- `drive`  -  by car (default). Austin, TX 30-minute isochrone: 6,262 for-sale homes
- `walk`  -  on foot. Austin, TX 30-minute isochrone: 1,777 for-sale homes

**Only these two modes actually work.** `cycle` and `public_transport` exist in the upstream
enum but are **unwired**: they are accepted and then silently ignored, returning the FULL
unfiltered result set as though no commute filter had been applied (verified  -  Austin for-sale
returns the same 7,425 at every interval, byte-identical to sending no commute at all).

This API rejects them with a 400 rather than pass that through, because a silently-unfiltered
page of results is far more damaging than an error: you would believe you were seeing homes
within a 30-minute bike ride and actually be seeing the whole metro.

Ignored unless BOTH `commute_lat` and `commute_lon` are supplied.

parameters.name: mls_status
parameters.description:
**Status the listing agent set in the source MLS**  -  a finer signal than `status`.

`status` is the Realtor.com lifecycle bucket (`for_sale`, `sold`, …); `mls_status` is what the
MLS itself reports, so it separates a genuinely available home from one already under contract
*inside the same bucket*.

**Case-sensitive.** The tokens are capitalised exactly as shown  -  lower-case `active` is
rejected. Counts are live Austin, TX matches:

- `Active`  -  on the market and taking offers (6,522 of the 7,593 `for_sale` listings)
- `Pending`  -  accepted offer, under contract (568 of the same 7,593)
- `Sold`  -  closed sale (92,033 of the 126,013 `sold` records  -  pair it with `status=sold`)

This is a CLOSED set of three: anything else hard-errors upstream and comes back as a 400.

Examples: `mls_status=Active` (skip everything under contract), `mls_status=Active,Pending`,
`status=sold&mls_status=Sold`.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

parameters.name: property_type
parameters.description:
**Primary property-type filter.**

- `single_family`  -  single-family houses
- `condos`  -  condominiums
- `townhomes`  -  townhouses / rowhouses
- `multi_family`  -  duplexes, triplexes and small apartment buildings
- `mobile`  -  mobile / manufactured homes
- `land`  -  land and vacant lots
- `farm`  -  farms and ranches
- `condo_townhome_rowhome_coop`  -  the combined condo/townhome/rowhome/co-op bucket
- `apartment`  -  apartment units (New York, NY: 121)
- `coop`  -  housing co-operatives (New York, NY: 8,193)
- `condop`  -  cond-ops, the NYC condo/co-op hybrid (New York, NY: 78)
- `duplex_triplex`  -  duplex / triplex (Los Angeles, CA: 3)
- `other`  -  anything else (New York, NY: 2)

**Not valid:** `townhouse` (the real token is `townhomes`) and `commercial` (accepted upstream but
returns 0 in every market). Unknown tokens return a 400 listing the valid values.

Full token list: `single_family`, `condos`, `townhomes`, `multi_family`, `mobile`, `land`, `farm`, `condo_townhome_rowhome_coop`, `apartment`, `coop`, `condop`, `duplex_triplex`, `other`.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description:
**Raw feature tags**, merged straight into the upstream tag filter.

**Warning  -  this is an OPEN vocabulary that is NOT validated upstream.** A typo or an
unrecognised tag does not raise an error: it silently returns **0 results**. (`zzz_not_a_tag`
returns 0, not a 400.)

**Use the five validated group parameters instead**  -  every token they accept is verified live,
and a bad one gets a helpful 400:
- `heating_cooling`  -  Central Air, Central Heat, Forced Air, Energy Efficient
- `home_features`  -  Fireplace, Hardwood Floors, Swimming Pool, Basement, …
- `lot_features`  -  Waterfront, Corner Lot, Cul de Sac, Lake View, …
- `community_features`  -  Community Pool, Clubhouse, Golf, Security, …
- `nyc_amenities`  -  Doorman, Elevator, Dishwasher, Outdoor Space

All five groups plus `tags` merge into ONE upstream tag array (union, de-duplicated), so they can
be mixed freely in a single request.

Only reach for `tags` when you need a tag you have actually seen in a `/search` response  -  every
result echoes its own `tags` array. Examples: `central_air`, `fireplace`, `swimming_pool`, `view`.

Multiple values allowed, but they are combined with **AND**  -  a listing must have EVERY value listed, so each extra value NARROWS the result set. (Verified in Austin, TX: `swimming_pool` alone ~1,100 listings, `fireplace` alone ~3,000, both together 696.) Comma-separated.

- `minimal`  -  low risk
- `moderate`  -  medium risk
- `severe`  -  high risk

Flood risk blends FEMA zone data with First Street flood modelling.

**Important:** this filters to listings AT the chosen tier, NOT "at most" that tier. To find
low-risk homes, pass `minimal`.

The five risk filters (`flood_risk`, `fire_risk`, `heat_risk`, `wind_risk`, `air_risk`) combine
into a single upstream filter, so they can be sent together.

detail. A name that matches nobody returns 0 results, not an error  -  so an empty response usually
means the spelling is off.

**Prefer `fulfillment_id` whenever you have it:** an advertiser id is stable and unambiguous,
while two agents can share a name and the same agent can be spelled differently across MLSs.

parameters.name: fulfillment_id
parameters.description:
**Realtor.com advertiser id of an agent**  -  the cleanest way to pull one agent's entire book of
business.

Unlike `selling_agent_name`, this works on EVERY status. Verified for agent `3809719`:

- `status=for_sale`  -  70 listings
- `status=for_rent`  -  10 listings
- `status=sold`  -  383 listings
- `status=off_market`  -  9 listings

Where to get one:

- `/agents-search`  -  every agent row echoes its own `fulfillment_id`
- any property detail  -  `advertisers[].fulfillment_id`

Examples: `fulfillment_id=3809719` (one agent), `fulfillment_id=3809719,1715146` (a whole team in a
single call).

An id that matches no listings returns 0 results rather than a 400  -  it is not validated against the
agent directory. `/agent-listings` is the dedicated endpoint for this filter.

Multiple values allowed  -  a listing matching **ANY** of them is returned (OR). Comma-separated.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
**Result ordering.** Default: `relevant` (Realtor.com relevance ranking).

- `relevant`  -  Realtor.com relevance (default)
- `newest`  -  most recently listed first
- `oldest`  -  longest on market first
- `price_low`  -  lowest price first
- `price_high`  -  highest price first
- `beds`  -  most bedrooms first
- `baths`  -  most bathrooms first
- `sqft`  -  largest living area first
- `lot_size`  -  largest lot first
- `year_built`  -  newest construction year first
- `sold_date`  -  most recently sold first (use with `status=sold`)

- `open_house`  -  soonest open house first

Exactly one ordering is applied: `relevant` uses the relevance ranker, any other alias uses an
explicit sort. They cannot be combined.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
**Page number, 1-indexed.** Default: `1`. Maximum: `500`.

The response echoes `page`, `page_size`, `total` and `total_pages`, so you can loop until
`page > total_pages`.

Deep paging is capped by `page * limit`; to walk a very large market, split it by ZIP, by price band
or by `lat`/`lon` radius instead of paging past the cap.
